subject: Re: Model fit & regression after v2.4 rollout - next steps
messages:
From: Sophia Zhang <sophia@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@retailco.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected quality drop after v2.4 rollout

Hi Marissa,

We spotted a noticeable drop in recommendation relevance after the v2.4 model rollout yesterday. About ~12% of the test prompts we routinely use now return less accurate product suggestions (examples attached). This is impacting a live personalization experiment.

Quick summary:
- A/B test traffic switched to v2.4 at 02:30 UTC on 2027-08-29
- Error appears most with short-context prompts and SKU disambiguation
- Repro steps and a small prompt set attached (retailco_test_prompts.csv)

Can we set up a quick follow-up? At minimum we need:
- a short post-call recap with next steps,
- your recommendation for model pinning/rollback, and
- a rough timeline for the fix or rollback.

We appreciate the quick help — this experiment is time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Sophia Zhang
Product Manager, Personalization
RetailCo

Attachments: retailco_test_prompts.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Zhang <sophia@retailco.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 17:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2.4 rollout

Hi Sophia — thanks for the heads up and for the prompt set, that was super helpful. Quick post-call recap and suggested next steps below.

Recap (from our call):
- You observed ~12% drop in relevance after v2.4; issues concentrated on short prompts and SKU disambiguation.
- RetailCo is currently running a time-sensitive personalization experiment and needs either a rollback or temporary pin while we investigate.
- You asked for recommended model variants and benchmark links to share with stakeholders.

Suggested next steps (proposed):
1) Immediate pin/rollback: our engineering team can pin your workspace to v2.3 or run a targeted rollback for your production traffic (we recommend pinning to v2.3 while we investigate).
2) Shared evals: we will run your prompt set through v2.3 and v2.4 and share a diff report (we'll attach regression_diff_20270829.pdf).
3) Short-term mitigation: if there are specific prompt patterns causing failure, we can provide prompt tuning suggestions and fallback routing to a stable model variant.
4) Timeline: preliminary diff + rollback plan within 6 hours; full investigation and fix ETA 48–72 hours (TBD based on root cause).

Recommended model options to consider (short list):
- rdw-gen-13b-v2.3 (current stable for RetailCo workloads)
- rdw-gen-13b-quant-q4/v2.3 (lower cost, similar quality for short prompts)
- open-llama-13b-q4 as a compatible fallback for SKU disambiguation workloads

Attachments I will upload: regression_diff_20270829.pdf (prelim), perf_benchmarks_20270829.html (benchmarks). I'm looping in Rishi and Priyom to own the rollback & investigation.

If you approve, we'll proceed to pin your deployment to v2.3 and run the diff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sophia Zhang <sophia@retailco.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 19:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2.4 rollout

Hi team — dug into the diff and wanted to share a concise technical summary. High-level findings:

1) Diff summary (prelim): the regression shows a pattern where v2.4's updated tokenization + attention remapping slightly changed prompt boundaries for short inputs, which in turn affected entity disambiguation. The largest deltas are in top-1 token probability in the first 6 tokens for these prompts. See attached regression_diff_20270829.pdf.

2) Root-cause hypothesis: an optimization in the compile/kernel selection path for short sequences (intended to reduce latency) changed how some prompt prefixes are handled. This trades a small latency gain for rare quality regression on edge prompt shapes.

3) Recommended immediate action: pin RetailCo workspace to rdw-gen-13b-v2.3 and run a canary rollback for 10% of traffic to verify. If canary looks good after 30 min, do full rollback.

4) Rollback logistics & timeline: I attached a rollback_plan_20270829.md with exact steps. Estimated time to canary: 45–60 minutes after approval; full rollback (if canary passes) ~2 hours. We'll also add a short-term scheduled job to re-run your prompt set nightly until the fix is merged.

5) Long-term: revert the specific short-sequence kernel selection tweak or add a policy that routes short-context requests to the previously stable kernel. We'll prioritize a fix but want to avoid frequent rollbacks.

I'll start the canary steps as soon as RetailCo approves pin/rollback.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
redwood.ai

Attachments: rollback_plan_20270829.md
